description: Comprehensive geological dataset describing a crystalline rock mass for hydraulic stimulation experiments is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Hannes Krietsch et al. High-resolution 3D geological models are used in underground development projects and corresponding numerical simulations with applications in e.g., tunneling, hydrocarbon exploration, geothermal exploitation and mining. Most geological models are based on sparse geological data sampled pointwise or along lines (e.g., boreholes), leading to oversimplified model geometries. Coverage: not stated; published in 2018. Formats: MATLAB, TXT, Image. The data are held in RWTH Aachen University and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: pages 1-12. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence of the data is not stated in the sources read (the paper itself is open access). Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked, and the coverage and resolution are those of the abstract only. It can support power-system, energy-planning and grid-operation studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
